summary: 8:30 AM ET run, published at 9:05 ET. Nothing settled: the only game left in week 2 is Giants at Rams tonight. Nothing closed: all three prop leans hold their numbers at the 8:58 capture, Terrance Ferguson under 32.5 receiving yards, Theo Johnson over 8.5 and Devin Singletary over 15.5. Nothing new published; the game lines still carry no lean and the three props are already out. The final injury report was read: none of the three players appears on it.
takeaways: Puka Nacua is questionable with a hip and Jordan Whittington doubtful with a quadricep on the Rams' final report, which is the first live use of yesterday's change: the projections now cut a questionable player to 75% of his share and remove a doubtful one, and this morning's snapshot records both. Worth saying plainly what that did to our own pick, since the Rams' targets have to go somewhere: Terrance Ferguson's projected receiving yards moved from 16.3 to 16.3, a tenth of a yard on the 80% range. A star receiver's share spread across a whole receiving corps barely touches a tight end's line. The injury logic is doing something real and something small, and both halves of that are worth knowing.

Inactives for a night game are out at 6:45 PM, which falls between the 5:30 and 11:30 runs, the same gap the Sunday late window had before yesterday. A Thursday, Sunday and Monday 6:50 PM run now covers it, so a night game can be priced on the inactive list rather than guessed at in the afternoon or missed entirely.

gameWatch.title: Rams receiving volume with Puka Nacua questionable
gameWatch.why: Nacua is questionable with a hip and Whittington doubtful with a quadricep, so the Rams could be down two receivers tonight. Our published Terrance Ferguson under 32.5 receiving yards is on the other side of that: if both sit, targets concentrate and a tight end is one of the places they land. The projection moved by a tenth of a yard, so this is a risk the model does not see rather than one it has priced.
gameWatch.needs: The 6:45 PM inactive list. The pick is graded as posted whatever it says; this is about what the next one should assume.
